title: How Much Rice Per Person: Dry and Cooked Amounts by Meal Type

seo.title: How Much Rice Per Person: Dry and Cooked Amounts
seo.meta_description: A practical starting point is 60–75 g dry rice per person as a side and 80–100 g when rice is the main starch. Cooking greatly increases weight and volume.
seo.search_intent: Calculate how much dry and cooked rice to prepare per person depending on whether rice is a side dish, main component, or part of a mixed recipe.

excerpt: There is no single correct rice portion. About 60–75 g dry per adult often works as a side dish, while 80–100 g is a more generous starting point when rice is the center of the meal. Rice absorbs water and may finish at roughly 2.5–3 times its dry weight.
content_html:
For most home meals, plan roughly 60–75 grams of dry rice per adult when it is a side dish and about 80–100 grams when rice is the main starch or bulk of the meal. These are planning ranges rather than a universal serving rule. A curry with rice on the side, a rice bowl, and a mixed rice dish with meat and vegetables all need different amounts.

The most useful habit is measuring before cooking. Rice absorbs a large amount of water and expands substantially, so comparing dry grams directly with cooked grams without accounting for hydration is misleading.

60–75 g dry works well for many side dishes

If the meal already includes a substantial amount of meat, fish, legumes, vegetables, or sauce, 60–75 g of dry rice often makes a reasonable adult side. Research on the Eetmaatje measuring cup cites 75 g dry rice per person as a reference from the Netherlands Nutrition Centre.

USDA yield tables also show how dramatic the expansion can be: one cup of dry long-grain rice can produce roughly 2.75 cups cooked. The exact yield changes with variety and technique, but it explains why a modest dry portion becomes a much larger cooked serving.

80–100 g makes more sense when rice is the centerpiece

For a rice bowl, fried rice, or a meal where rice supplies most of the starch and bulk, 80–100 g dry is a more realistic starting point for many adults. The same Eetmaatje research notes 100 g as a reference for larger appetites.

That does not mean everyone needs that amount. A child, a small appetite, or a meal with several courses will need less, while a very active person or one-dish meal may call for more.

Cooked weight depends on how much water the rice holds

As a broad guide, 70 g of dry rice may finish around 175–210 g cooked. The range is intentionally wide because basmati, jasmine, brown rice, risotto rice, and rice that is boiled and drained do not retain exactly the same amount of water.

That is why dry weight is more reliable for shopping and meal planning. If you only have cooked rice, roughly 180–220 g can represent a moderate main-meal portion, but no one conversion works for every rice and cooking method.

Mixed rice dishes usually need less rice per person

Paella-style dishes, chicken and rice, and vegetable rice contain other ingredients that add volume and satiety. If you calculate 100 g of dry rice per person on top of generous protein and vegetables, you can easily produce excessive leftovers.

For these dishes, 60–80 g per person is often a more cautious starting point. Risotto is different because rice remains the central ingredient even when stock, cheese, mushrooms, or vegetables are added, so the dry amount may still sit nearer 70–90 g.

For a crowd, calculate by weight rather than cups

Cups are convenient, but rice types pack differently and volume errors multiply when cooking for ten or twenty people. Using grams is simple: 70 g × 8 people equals 560 g of dry rice.

Reduce that figure if there are children, appetizers, or several side dishes. Increase it if rice is the whole meal and you know the group has larger appetites. For an event, a small margin is sensible, but there is no need to double the quantity “just in case.”

The practical rule: think 60–75 g dry for a side and 80–100 g when rice is the star. Multiply by the number of people, adjust for the rest of the menu, and remember the cooked grain will weigh several times more because of absorbed water.

These quantities are a starting point rather than a rigid rule. Food size, recipe, appetite, side dishes, and cooking method all change the result. If you make the dish regularly, note what worked in your kitchen: your own repeatable reference is often more useful than one number applied to every situation.

faq.question: How much dry rice per person?
faq.answer: About 60–75 g as a side dish and roughly 80–100 g when rice is the main starch.

faq.question: How much does rice weigh after cooking?
faq.answer: Often around 2.5–3 times the dry amount, although rice type and cooking method change the exact water uptake.

faq.question: How much rice for four people?
faq.answer: As a guide, 240–300 g dry for a side or 320–400 g if rice is the main component.
